query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A machine-learning-based potential can be developed to predict the free energies of both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems near phase transitions, with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained, at a significantly reduced computational cost compared to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy systems, including elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems, in solid and fluid states near phase transitions
generation.intervention: Development of a machine-learning-based potential using a dataset of ab initio calculations for a range of high-entropy systems
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions near phase transitions, with temperatures ranging from 500 K to 2000 K
generation.structural_mediator: The machine-learning-based potential will mediate the structural properties of the high-entropy systems, including the arrangement of atoms and the resulting free energies
generation.mechanism: The machine-learning-based potential will learn the complex relationships between the atomic structure and the free energies of the high-entropy systems, allowing for accurate predictions of thermodynamic properties
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in computational cost of at least 50% compared to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, while maintaining an accuracy of at least 90% in predicting phase free energies and derived observables
generation.baseline: Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD
generation.boundary: The proposed method is expected to be applicable to high-entropy systems with up to 5 components, and temperatures ranging from 500 K to 2000 K
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the machine-learning-based potential may be limited by the quality and quantity of the training data, and the complexity of the high-entropy systems being studied

falsification_experiment.design: A benchmark study comparing the predictions of the machine-learning-based potential to those of explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD for a range of high-entropy systems
measurements: Derived observables such as entropy and heat capacity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine-learning-based potential fails to predict the phase free energies and derived observables with an accuracy of at least 90% compared to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD for at least 80% of the benchmark systems, the hypothesis is falsified
